basis: Cataracts, skin/hair disease and oral inflammation define syndrome; myopathy in 1/1 assessed; developmental delay in 1/2 omitted by cap.
Defined by intellectual disability; developmental delay and seizures are neurologic manifestations.
Koolen-de Vries neurodevelopmental syndrome; additional congenital anomalies are variable and not established here as common organ damage.
Brain malformations, developmental impairment and arthrogryposis define disease; neonatal respiratory distress alone does not establish direct lung damage.
Clonal marrow disease with myelodysplasia and macrocytic anemia; infections and leukemia are minority complications.
Inflammation surrounding bile ducts; no specific infectious or immune-mediated mechanism established.
Progressive cerebellar degeneration; macular degeneration and ptosis are frequent (30-79%); abnormal eye movements alone are neurologic.
Intestinal trehalase deficiency causes a defined digestive enzyme defect and carbohydrate malabsorption after trehalose exposure.
Dentin and dental root abnormalities with pulp obliteration and tooth loss; teeth belong to the gastrointestinal axis.
Exposed malformed brain with absent or deficient cranial vault defines exencephaly; proptosis alone does not establish ocular damage.
Fatty-acid oxidation disorder encompassing CPT1A and CPT2 deficiencies; hepatic, cardiac and skeletal muscle injury vary substantially by subtype.
Invasive carcinoma arising in urinary bladder urothelium; bladder belongs to the renal axis.
Eye, dental and digital defects define disease; neurologic deficits frequent (30-79%); bladder dysfunction (12/20), hearing loss and hair defects omitted by cap.
Dysraphic lipomatous malformation attached to the spinal cord; associated vertebral abnormalities have no established frequency.
Selenoprotein N-related congenital myopathy affects skeletal muscle; respiratory insufficiency reflects respiratory muscle weakness rather than direct lung damage.
Benign peripheral nerve sheath tumor; epithelioid morphology does not change its tissue of origin.
Meier-Gorlin skeletal and external-ear malformation syndrome; renal hypoplasia in 1/1 reported patient, with very limited subtype evidence.
Skin/hair disease with immune dysfunction; isolated reports of gut, renal, hearing or CNS findings do not establish damage in >=30% of patients.
Fetal enterovirus infection; supplied evidence does not establish a particular organ lesion as defining or present in >=30%.
Left ventricular noncompaction is a structural myocardial disorder.
Developmental impairment defines syndrome; dental and skeletal defects 80-99%, ptosis 5/7; hypertension (30-79%) omitted by cap.
Inherited retinal signaling disorder causing stationary night blindness and reduced visual acuity.
Benign ovarian epithelial adenoma; reproductive tissue origin without a defined endocrine disorder lies outside the axes.
Inherited renal tubular amino-acid transport defect causing cystine wasting and urinary stone formation.
Inherited glomerular disease with steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome, focal segmental glomerulosclerosis and frequent kidney failure.
